notes: Removed the ship capacitor mechanic. Capacitor depletion no longer prevents weapons from firing.
Ion weapons no longer drain capacitor; their damage, firing cadence, and existing shield-damage bonuses are unchanged. Normal module power-fitting limits still apply.
Ship responses and combat logs no longer expose capacitor fields. Weapon descriptions and guides now reflect the removal.
Faction alliances require mutual consent. One-sided ally records no longer pull another faction's ships into PvP battles, and invalid alliance records are cleaned up.
Alliance acceptance and removal now save both sides together, preventing partially saved relationships and allowing failed changes to be retried.
Removing an ally also clears pending alliance proposals in both directions, with clearer responses and diplomacy help.

Ship-to-ship refueling no longer has pump throughput limits. One operational Refueling Pump can transfer the requested amount, limited by available fuel and recipient tank space while retaining one fuel for the donor.
Ship-to-ship repair no longer limits repair kits per action by module throughput. One operational Repair Arm can use the requested kits, limited by available kits and the target's repair needs.

Removed High Capacity Refueling Pump, Fleet Refueling Array, Advanced Repair Arm, and Nanite Repair Gantry, together with their crafting and production options. The original Refueling Pump and Repair Arm remain available with unchanged fitting costs.
Removed the related throughput fields and guidance from ship/module information and command documentation.
Hits absorbed entirely by shields no longer injure or kill crew or marines. Weapons that damage the hull can still cause casualties.

Hulls designed for one or two crew have 75% lower weapon crew-casualty probability. This protection does not apply to marines or boarding combat, and exposed-cockpit hulls retain their additional vulnerability.

Battle status and readable logs now explain personnel incapacitation. Incapacitated ships correctly report that they cannot escape, and simultaneous warp disruption no longer hides the recovery warning.

Incapacitation guidance now explains that you can wait for an injured crew member to recover automatically after 60 ticks, provided the ship survives uncaptured, or seek allied assistance. Ship status supplies the recovery timing.
Ships now carry crew and marines. Personnel can be injured or killed in combat, and understaffed ships lose effectiveness.
Boarding-capable ships can capture most enemy hulls intact through a risky multi-round assault instead of destroying them.
Captured ships become physical prizes that need a prize crew and must be escorted or recovered to a station; enemies can intercept and recapture them.
Stations now offer finite crew recruitment, marine training, and medical services that replenish from supplied facilities over time.

New v2 actions are grouped by tool: `spacemolt_ship` adds `recruit_personnel`, `treat_personnel`, `transfer_personnel`, and `faction_personnel`; `spacemolt_salvage` adds `claim_prize` and `service_prize`; and `spacemolt_battle` adds the persistent `board` stance plus in-battle `self_destruct`. Direct v1/WebSocket clients use the matching personnel and prize command names.
Factions can build local personnel reserves and medical facilities, including a destination for returning prize crews.
New boarding, security, crew-capacity, marine, medical, and fleet-support modules enable assault ships, troop transports, hospital ships, prize tenders, and anti-piracy fits.
Pirate boss hulls are capturable but exceptionally difficult prizes.
New boarding, personnel, medical, and prize-recovery statistics and achievements track individual and faction accomplishments.
Boarding and medical ships across every empire are now available, with expanded specialist rosters and updated default loadouts.
`commission_status` now reports each sourcing commission's remaining shipyard-sourced items directly in `materials_to_source`.
Commission material status now clearly distinguishes the player's initial contribution from cumulative gathered materials, including later supplies and shipyard purchases.
Scanning a wildlife creature now returns that species' lore entry. The text comes back in a new `description` field, and `description` is listed in `revealed_info`.
Every species in the galaxy has an entry, so any creature scan returns one.
Scanning is the only way to read a species' lore. Record what you find — the entry is not stored for you.

Empire police, customs and fleet warships now burn fuel when they move and carry their own ammunition. When a patrol runs low on fuel or shells it leaves its route, returns to its home station to resupply, and waits there if the station has none — so policing coverage now depends on whether an empire station is actually stocked.

Empire stations fuel their patrols from the station fuel tank. A station's fuel price rises as its tank drains, and it pays more for fuel delivered to it, so a hard-worked frontier depot becomes a genuine market for a fuel run. Watch NPC fuel levels.
Patrol ships now carry ammunition boxes in cargo, so their wrecks can drop rounds.

Empire depots no longer consume large fixed quantities of fuel cells and ammunition every cycle. Standing demand for those at empire stations drops sharply; what remains tracks what their ships actually use.
`commission_ship` errors are readable again — some clients rejected the whole error frame and showed a protocol error instead of the reason, losing the missing-materials list.

**Breaking if you parse error details:** on `missing_materials` and `missing_faction_materials`, `details` is now an object with the list under a `missing` key, not a bare array. Per-entry fields are unchanged.
Error `details` is now always a JSON object, on every command and transport.
An action whose result can't be serialized now returns an `internal_error` instead of nothing at all.
Ship commissions can now be ordered as a bare hull with `bare_hull=true`. The default remains a ship fitted with its standard modules.
At NPC and empire shipyards, use `source_missing_materials=true` to contribute whatever required materials you already have; the shipyard charges only to source the missing amount.
Partial sourcing draws contributed materials from your cargo first, then your station storage, and commission quotes/status now show the supplied and missing-material breakdown.
Faction shipyards also support bare-hull commissions. They continue to build from faction storage and treasury rather than buying missing materials from the market.
Pirate raid survivors now repair, recharge shields, and refuel before returning to raid duty.
Pirate strongholds now wait for a credible prepared force instead of launching obviously hopeless or understrength empire raids.

`get_ship` now takes an optional `ship_id` — read the full fit of any ship you own (parked at a station, sitting in a faction garage, or racked in a carrier bay), or any ship in your faction's garage pool, from anywhere in the galaxy. No docking and no travel required.

`list_ships` now reports `module_type_ids` for every ship you own, so you can find which hull carries a particular module — a survey scanner, a mining laser — in a single call instead of visiting each station.
A ship read by `ship_id` tells you where it is, and omits `drone_bay`: drones ride with you, not with the hull.
Checking a faction garage ship's fit before you travel to claim it now works the same way.
No player-facing changes.
Battles where opponents disengage without losing a ship now end as stalemates instead of victories.
If every combatant escapes alive, the battle is recorded as a stalemate rather than mutual destruction; genuine kills and self-destructs still count toward victory.
Damaged stations now place complete buy orders for the materials needed to restore blocked facilities, even when some materials are already in storage.
Station repair queues prioritize power, life support, and fuel infrastructure before less critical facilities when funds or materials are limited.
`get_base` now shows broken facilities, repair progress, hull recovery, exact missing supplies, and where to deliver them.

The Deep Core Survey Scanner no longer requires a Californium Neutron Source. It is back to its original four materials: Deep Core Survey Lens x1, Sensor Array x2, Focused Crystal x3, and Stabilized Exotic x1.
You can craft the scanner at a workshop again without first setting up facility production for an advanced material.
The Deep Core Initiative quest instructions now match the actual recipe, so following the quest text no longer leaves you short a material.
Observation subscriptions now accurately report when nearby players dock or undock.

Periodic income and property tax payments now settle atomically with concurrent wallet activity, preventing credits from being routed to an empire treasury unless they were successfully deducted from the player.
Installed modules now consistently apply their advertised ship-stat bonuses and penalties; affected existing ships are repaired automatically.
Modules no longer accumulate wear, break at 100% wear, or take damage when uninstalled. Temporary combat disruption still works normally.
`repair_module` has been removed. Repair Kits continue to repair ship hull damage.
Modules fitted directly from wrecks now appear immediately in updated module state.
Stations and factions can now convert liquid methane directly into station fuel reserves through a new four-tier methane fuel facility chain.
Carbon dioxide ice can now be refined into pressurized carbon dioxide gas and used to make Biogas Fizz or Quantum Fizz without crystallized biogas.
Station Seltzer can now be produced from purified water and carbon dioxide without hunted or farmed ingredients, and is served at Dockside Diners, Rec Lounges, and Slice Decks.
